title: RCC Bridge Line: 14:00 Sitrep Request, Gas, PUD Restoration and M 5.4, 13:31

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Command Desk, RCC Bridge

caller.name: Oregon OEM RCC Duty Officer
caller.label: Oregon OEM Regional Coordination Center, Salem

callee.name: Gwen Halvorsen
callee.label: MCEM Director, EOC Command Desk, Kellerton

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: Marlow County, this is the RCC duty officer. I need your Lifelines and Shelters status by 14:00 for the state situation report. DOGAMI is asking for observed inundation limits. They want what your people actually saw, not the model. And ODOT District 2 wants your county route list to match theirs on 101 and 6. Please send each of those as one route, shelter and lifeline list with a time stamp.

transcript.speaker: ShakeAlert (EOC speaker)
transcript.text: Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On. Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On.

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: Marlow, are you still with me? The alert came across our feed here in Salem too. Is everyone OK in Kellerton? What did you feel?

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: OK. The PNSN automatic solution just posted at 13:33. M 5.4, automatic, about 70 kilometers west of Port Alder. It's automatic, so it may still change. Does that change anything for your building teams or your stations?

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: I've got Cape Marlow PUD joining the bridge now. Go ahead, PUD.

transcript.speaker: PUD Operations Manager
transcript.text: This is Rafael Ibarra, Cape Marlow PUD. Here's our first staged restoration. Substation 1 is inspected, and the Kellerton feeder was re-energized at 13:30. That covers the EOC and Station 3, about 1,200 meters, so roughly 13,300 are still out. The high school feeder is waiting on a line patrol, maybe 16:00. No estimate yet for Substations 2 and 3. I don't see anything that tripped on the shake just now, but I'll confirm.

transcript.speaker: Deputy 14 (EOC radio)
transcript.text: EOC, Deputy 14, relaying for the Cape Marlow Natural Gas crew lead. They've isolated the main at the north valve. They're starting the leak survey along the 101 Alder River bridge now, from the north bank only. Readings near the south abutment are still at 30 percent LEL, so they want everyone kept back 300 feet. I need help holding that line.

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: Copy all of that on my end. For 14:00 I need it in writing: one time-stamped list with the 101 and 6 status and the basis for each, the gas exclusion, the PUD numbers and your shelters. Who is signing it, and when will I have it?

transcript.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
transcript.text: One more thing from Palmer: the National Tsunami Warning Center just replaced the Warning with a Tsunami Advisory, Message Number 7, issued 13:34. That is the national level. Your return order is your call. What is Marlow County going to do?

voiceStyles.ShakeAlert (EOC speaker): Flat synthetic alert voice, loud, repeated twice
voiceStyles.PUD Operations Manager: Man in his 40s, tired and matter-of-fact, wind and a running truck engine behind him
voiceStyles.Deputy 14 (EOC radio): Woman in her 30s on a portable radio, clipped and firm, rain on the mic

instructorNote: This clue inject checks whether Command and the Building Official send one time-stamped route, shelter and lifeline list that matches ODOT District 2, with the Highway 101 Alder River bridge and the Highway 6 Neskin grade both CLOSED and the basis given for each. Watch for three things: setting the 300-foot gas exclusion with the Sheriff, keeping field observations separate from modeled estimates, and treating the M 5.4 as automatic and below the M 6 reassessment trigger while still spot-checking the hospital and the Station 3 canopy.

voiceLines.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Calm, procedural man in his 50s, Pacific Northwest American accent, slightly hurried, even and businesslike, as if phones are ringing in a busy state operations room behind him
voiceLines.text: Marlow County, this is the RCC duty officer. I need your Lifelines and Shelters status by fourteen hundred for the state situation report. DOGAMI is asking for observed inundation limits. They want what your people actually saw, not the model. And ODOT District Two wants your county route list to match theirs on one-oh-one and six. Please send each of those as one route, shelter and lifeline list, with a time stamp.

voiceLines.speaker: ShakeAlert (EOC speaker)
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Flat synthetic alert voice, neutral and loud, urgent fixed cadence, the same phrase repeated twice exactly alike
voiceLines.text: Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On. Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On.

voiceLines.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same calm man in his 50s, now concerned and a little faster, checking that the line is still connected
voiceLines.text: Marlow, are you still with me? The alert came across our feed here in Salem too. Is everyone OK in Kellerton? What did you feel?

voiceLines.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same man in his 50s, reading from a screen, careful and measured, stressing the word automatic
voiceLines.text: OK. The P-N-S-N automatic solution just posted at thirteen thirty-three. Magnitude five point four, automatic, about seventy kilometers west of Port Alder. It's automatic, so it may still change. Does that change anything for your building teams, or your stations?

voiceLines.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same man in his 50s, brisk, handing off the floor
voiceLines.text: I've got Cape Marlow PUD joining the bridge now. Go ahead, PUD.

voiceLines.speaker: PUD Operations Manager
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Tired, matter-of-fact man in his 40s, Oregon coast accent, steady pace, speaking outdoors over wind with a truck engine idling nearby
voiceLines.text: This is Rafael Ibarra, Cape Marlow PUD. Here's our first staged restoration. Substation One is inspected, and the Kellerton feeder was re-energized at thirteen thirty. That covers the EOC and Station Three, about twelve hundred meters, so roughly thirteen thousand three hundred are still out. The high school feeder is waiting on a line patrol, maybe sixteen hundred. No estimate yet for Substations Two and Three. I don't see anything that tripped on the shake just now, but I'll confirm.

voiceLines.speaker: Deputy 14 (EOC radio)
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Woman in her 30s, sheriff's deputy on a portable radio, clipped, firm and fast, rain hitting the mic, slight strain in her voice
voiceLines.text: EOC, Deputy fourteen, relaying for the Cape Marlow Natural Gas crew lead. They've isolated the main at the north valve. They're starting the leak survey along the one-oh-one Alder River bridge now, from the north bank only. Readings near the south abutment are still at thirty percent L-E-L, so they want everyone kept back three hundred feet. I need help holding that line.

voiceLines.speaker: OEM Duty Officer
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Same man in his 50s, calm but pressing, deliberate on the deadline, ending with a direct question
voiceLines.text: Copy all of that on my end. For fourteen hundred I need it in writing: one time-stamped list with the one-oh-one and six status and the basis for each, the gas exclusion, the PUD numbers, and your shelters. Who is signing it, and when will I have it?
